name: core-data-lib
summary: A reflection-once, annotation-driven data access library for PostgreSQL over R2DBC. Define an entity, extend a repository base class, and get filtering, sorting, free-text search, pagination and joined relations for free, with hand-rolled parameterized SQL underneath instead of JPA/Hibernate. Published on Maven Central as a drop-in Spring Boot autoconfiguration.
problem: Reactive Spring Boot services on R2DBC/Postgres have no JPA/Hibernate equivalent. Every entity that needs filtering, sorting, search, pagination, or joins ends up with hand-rolled, repeated, easy-to-get-wrong parameterized SQL.
approach: Built a small annotation-driven library with a reflection-once entity scanner, a composable filter/query API, a SQL builder that only joins tables a query actually touches, and a typed exception layer over Postgres SQLSTATEs, then wired it into Spring Boot as a zero-config autoconfiguration module.
architecture:
Two API layers share one execution engine. The high-level path, `Query<T>`, `Filters`, and `AbstractReactiveRepository`, is what a consuming service uses day to day: annotate an entity with `@Table`/`@Column`/`@Id`/`@Join`, extend the repository base class, and get parameterized CRUD, arbitrary filter trees, multi-field search, sorting, offset pagination and conditionally-joined relations for free. A join declared on the entity is only added to the generated SQL when a query actually references the field it's attached to.

The low-level path, `QueryContext`, `SqlBuilder`, `QueryExecutor`, is the same engine exposed directly, for callers who want to hand-build a query without going through the repository abstraction. A blocking facade sits on top of the reactive API for callers not on Project Reactor.

Every failure mode surfaces as one of eighteen typed `DatabaseException` subtypes, mapped from PostgreSQL SQLSTATEs (unique/foreign-key/check/exclusion violations, deadlocks, timeouts, permission errors, connection failures) rather than an opaque driver exception. Callers can catch the base type or discriminate by subtype, and every repository call reports failure as a reactive `onError` signal rather than throwing synchronously.

The whole library wires into a consuming service through Spring Boot's own autoconfiguration mechanism (`CommonDbAutoConfiguration`, registered via `AutoConfiguration.imports`) with every bean marked `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`, so any piece, down to the field resolver, can be overridden by declaring a bean of the same type.
outcome: Published, versioned library on Maven Central (`io.github.alexdev93:core-data-lib`) with a CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions) that auto-publishes snapshots from `develop` and cuts GPG-signed releases from tagged branches on `main`, following Gitflow.

decisions.title: Hand-rolled SQL over JPA/Hibernate
decisions.detail: Reactive Spring Boot on R2DBC has no JPA/Hibernate equivalent, so the library generates parameterized SQL directly rather than adopting an ORM that doesn't support the reactive stack.

decisions.title: Reflection-once entity scanning
decisions.detail: An entity's @Table/@Column/@Join metadata is read once via reflection and cached, not re-inspected on every query.

decisions.title: Conditional joins
decisions.detail: A join declared on an entity is only added to the generated SQL when a query actually references the joined field, so a plain SELECT that never touches it stays join-free.

decisions.title: Gitflow release process
decisions.detail: develop auto-publishes a -SNAPSHOT to Maven Central on every push; a tagged main release is GPG-signed and published via GitHub Actions: a moving target to track plus a stable, signed release train.

guide:
[![Maven Central](https://img.shields.io/maven-central/v/io.github.alexdev93/core-data-lib.svg?label=Maven%20Central)](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/io.github.alexdev93/core-data-lib)
[![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0)
[![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-17%2B-orange.svg)](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/io.github.alexdev93/core-data-lib)

A reflection-once, annotation-driven data-access library for PostgreSQL over R2DBC, for anyone who wants to actually use it in a Spring Boot + R2DBC + PostgreSQL service, not just read about it.

## Requirements

- Java 17+
- Maven 3.9+ (or Gradle 8+)
- A consuming service already using Spring Boot 3.x/4.x with R2DBC

## Install

Released versions are published on Maven Central, so no extra repository configuration is needed.

**Maven** (`pom.xml`):

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.github.alexdev93</groupId>
    <artifactId>core-data-lib</artifactId>
    <version>0.1.0</version>
</dependency>

<!-- the actual Postgres R2DBC driver; core-data-lib only depends on the R2DBC SPI -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.postgresql</groupId>
    <artifactId>r2dbc-postgresql</artifactId>
</dependency>
```

**Gradle** (`build.gradle`):

```groovy
dependencies {
    implementation 'io.github.alexdev93:core-data-lib:0.1.0'
    implementation 'org.postgresql:r2dbc-postgresql'
}
```

Tracking unreleased changes: `develop` publishes a `-SNAPSHOT` build to Central on every push (auto-expires after 90 days). Snapshots need the Central snapshot repository added explicitly, since Maven doesn't search snapshot repos by default:

```xml
<repositories>
    <repository>
        <id>central-snapshots</id>
        <url>https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots/</url>
        <releases><enabled>false</enabled></releases>
        <snapshots><enabled>true</enabled></snapshots>
    </repository>
</repositories>
```

The autoconfiguration is picked up automatically via Spring Boot's standard `AutoConfiguration.imports` mechanism, so no `@Import` or `@ComponentScan` changes are needed.

## Connect the database

Standard Spring Boot R2DBC config; the library doesn't invent its own connection mechanism:

```yaml
spring:
  r2dbc:
    url: r2dbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/mydb
    username: postgres
    password: secret
```

## Define an entity and a repository

```java
@Table(value = "users", alias = "u", defaultSort = "createdAt", defaultSortDirection = SortDirection.DESC)
public class User {

    @Id
    private UUID id;

    @Column(filterable = true, sortable = true, searchable = true)
    private String email;

    @Column(searchable = true, searchMode = SearchMode.STARTS_WITH)
    private String fullName;

    private Instant createdAt; // @Column is optional, defaults to filterable+sortable+selectable

    public User() {} // required, rows are mapped back via reflection
}

@Repository
public class UserRepository extends AbstractReactiveRepository<User, UUID> {
    public UserRepository(QueryExecutor executor) {
        super(User.class, executor);
    }
}
```

`QueryExecutor` is injected by Spring; nothing else to wire.

## CRUD, filter, sort, search, paginate

```java
userRepository.save(user);          // inserts if user.getId() == null, else updates by id
userRepository.findById(id);        // Mono<User>
userRepository.deleteById(id);      // Mono<Void>

Query<User> query = Query.of(User.class)
        .filter(Filters.eq("status", "ACTIVE"))
        .search("john", "email", "fullName")
        .sortBy("createdAt", DESC)
        .page(0, 20);

userRepository.findPage(query);     // Mono<PageResult<User>>
```

`Filters` covers every operator: `eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, like, startsWith, endsWith, in, notIn, between, isNull, isNotNull`, plus `and()`/`or()` for nested groups. `Query<T>` also builds straight from a JSON-bindable `QueryParams` for a `@ModelAttribute`-style REST endpoint.

## Joined relations

Declare the join once on the entity, reference it from a field. It's only added to the generated SQL when a query actually touches that field:

```java
@Table(value = "orders", alias = "o", joins = {
        @Join(name = "customer", table = "customers", alias = "c", on = "o.customer_id = c.id")
})
public class Order {
    @Column(join = "customer", name = "c.name", filterable = true, sortable = true)
    private String customerName;
}
```

## Not on Project Reactor?

```java
Repository<User, UUID> blocking = userRepository.blocking();
User user = blocking.findById(id).orElseThrow();
```

## Exception handling

Everything thrown is a `DatabaseException` subtype. Catch the base type or discriminate by subtype (`QueryValidationException`, `RecordNotFoundException`, `DatabaseDuplicateKeyException`, `ForeignKeyException`, `DeadlockException`, `QueryTimeoutDatabaseException`, and more). All of it surfaces as a reactive `onError` signal, never a synchronous throw:

```java
userRepository.findPage(query)
        .onErrorResume(QueryValidationException.class,
                ex -> Mono.error(new ResponseStatusException(BAD_REQUEST, ex.getMessage())));
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| `No qualifying bean of type 'DatabaseClient'` | Added `spring-data-r2dbc` instead of `spring-boot-starter-data-r2dbc`; only the starter activates the autoconfiguration this library builds on. |
| Snapshot dependency won't resolve | Missing the `central-snapshots` repository block. Maven doesn't search Central's snapshot repo by default. |
| `field not filterable/sortable/searchable` | The field's `@Column` doesn't set the attribute you're using it for. |
| A join doesn't show up in the generated SQL | Joins are only added when a query references a field marked `join = "..."`. A plain SELECT that never touches it won't pull it in. |

## Getting the code

The library itself needs no repo access; it's a published, versioned Maven Central artifact, usable in any Spring Boot + R2DBC + Postgres project without ever touching the source.

The source repository ([github.com/alexdev93/common-db](https://github.com/alexdev93/common-db)) is currently **private**. To read the code, file an issue, or open a pull request, reach out with what you'd like to do (review the code, report a bug, propose a feature) so access can be scoped appropriately: **alemayehu.dev@gmail.com**.
